section.comment: `##` opens a section heading (spec: comment text is markdown). Since 2026-10-12 it is scoped as a comment as well as a heading, so a theme that paints no heading still paints it as the comment it is, and it ends at its line's end, where the lexer ends it. A tab inside it is legal, as in any comment, and is not painted; a raw control character is refused there and is.
section.name: comment.line.double-number-sign.hero markup.heading.hero

comment.comment: A comment directly above a declaration is its documentation. A region since 2026-10-12, so the raw control characters the lexer refuses inside a comment are painted there (spec § 1); a tab, which a comment holds, is not.
comment.name: comment.line.number-sign.hero

tab.comment: A tab is a compile error everywhere but inside a comment (spec § 1; design.md §4.15): `tab_in_indentation`, `tab_in_line`, and `raw_tab` inside a literal. The two comment rules come first in the list and take their whole line, so a tab inside a comment never reaches this rule. Written `\x09` and never `\t`, which the check's own reader refuses.
tab.name: invalid.illegal.tab.hero

control.comment: A raw control character, the tab and the line feed aside: refused in code (`unexpected_character`), in a comment, a string, an `f` literal's text and a character literal (`invisible_character`, panel 192's R2 and R3). The bidirectional controls, U+2028 and U+2029 are refused too and are not painted here: their pattern needs `\x{…}`, which the check's reader does not run.
control.name: invalid.illegal.control-character.hero

foreign.comment: spec/reserved-words.md — keywords imported from another language. Marked INVALID on purpose: the editor shows the mistake before the compiler does. `use` was in this list and is a Heroes keyword, so every module line in every file showed as an error; it now sits in #keyword, where the spec puts it (`a module is named with use`). The list is otherwise the spec's own table, word for word. Corrected 2026-10-12: the table it copied had no row for `int`, which `selfhost/keywords.hero`'s `declared_word` has refused since `selfhost/` was born, so this list never painted it. The list is now the words of `declared_word`'s arms, which the `spec/colouring` check holds it to, and the registry's rows are held to the same arms.
foreign.name: invalid.illegal.foreign-keyword.hero

keyword.comment: spec/reserved-words.md's closing paragraph, and selfhost/keywords.hero::keyword. `true` and `false` were filed under #builtin-type, which is where a value is not: both tables call them keywords.
keyword.name: keyword.control.hero

use.comment: `as` is a contextual word (`selfhost/keywords.hero`'s `contextual()`), read by the parser only after a `use` line's path (spec § 1, `Use`), so it is painted only there: a column-0 `use`, its path, a space, then `as`. Anywhere else `as` is a name. A `use` line without `as` is painted by #keyword.

extern.comment: An `extern` group (spec § 13, `Extern`): a column-0 `extern` line and the lines below it, up to the first line whose first character is neither a space nor `#`, so a blank line or a column-0 comment does not end it, the same rule `site/src/lib/highlight.ts` follows. `link` and `package` are painted only right after the header's string on the `extern` line; the group's other contextual words only on its indented lines (#extern-member).

extern-member.comment: One indented line of an `extern` group, where the parser reads the marks of `Member` and `CParam` (spec § 13): each painted unless the next character that is not a space is `:`, so a parameter or a field named `owned` stays a name. These are the eleven contextual words besides `as`, `link` and `package`.

rest-zero.comment: `rest` and `zero` are contextual words (`selfhost/keywords.hero`'s `contextual()`), read by the parser together and in one place: a labelled argument whose label is `rest` and whose value is the bare name `zero`, ending a call's list, is the words that end a construction of a group's record (spec § 13, `selfhost/parse/rest_words.hero`). So both are painted only there: after a `(` or a `,`, or opening a line of a broken list, and before a `,`, a `)`, a comment or the line's end, which is where an argument whose value is a bare name ends. Anywhere else each is a name, `zero` a binding like any other (defect 401). A field or a parameter named `rest` whose type is called `zero` would be painted too, which a line alone cannot tell apart; no program in the repository has one.

declaration.comment: `function dist2(…)` / `record Point` — the kind opens the line, the name follows (panel 018). Since 2026-10-12 the kind is painted here, before #keyword reaches it, and the name by its kind: a function, a type, a constant. The `extern` prefix this rule allowed is gone: an `extern` line opens a group and its members are indented declarations (spec § 13). Since panel 217 (M-readonly-lend) a function's line runs to its end here, so `lent` after a parameter's type, the next character a `,` or a `)`, is painted the contextual word the parser reads there; a parameter named `lent` is followed by `:` and stays a name.

builtin-type.comment: spec/heroes-spec.md § Types, the whole table. This read `int|f64|bool|str|ptr|cstr` and so coloured a word the language does not have while leaving every sized integer plain: `i64` is what a program actually writes, and it was the one type never highlighted. `[T]`, `{K: V}` and `T?` are shapes rather than words and are built out of these. Since 2026-10-12 not after `.` or `::`, where the word is a field's name.
builtin-type.name: support.type.hero

hole.comment: `???` is a valid expression, not an error (§4.16)
hole.name: markup.italic.hole.hero

string.comment: A string is one line (spec § 1), so it ends at its closing quote or at the line's end, where the lexer refuses it as `unterminated_string`; until 2026-10-12 a string left open painted every line after it as text.
string.name: string.quoted.double.hero

patterns.comment: spec § 2: five in a string, `\n` `\t` `\r` `\\` `\"`. This read `[nt\\"]` and said `exactly these four` until 2026-09-13, so a legal `\r` fell through to the rule below and a CORRECT program was painted `invalid.illegal`. Measured the day it was fixed: `print("a\rb")` runs at exit 0. `spec/heroes-spec.md:39` and `selfhost/escape.hero`'s `escape_text` are the two sides the `spec/colouring` check now holds together.
patterns.name: constant.character.escape.hero

patterns.comment: panel 192's R5: a character a line cannot show (a control character, a bidirectional control, U+2028 or U+2029) is written by its code, `\u{1b}`, in lowercase hexadecimal with no leading zero, its one spelling, of a code that names a character: a Unicode scalar value, never a surrogate (d800 to dfff) and nothing past 10ffff, which the compiler refuses as no escape (until 2026-10-07 this painted both, defect 377). Which characters a string must write by code is the compiler's to say (`selfhost/code_escape.hero`), so this paints every such code in the one spelling as an escape, and every other spelling falls to the rule below, as the compiler refuses it. The alternatives are by count of digits: one to three, four outside the surrogates, five, and six from 10
patterns.name: constant.character.escape.hero

patterns.comment: the backslash is reserved — anything else is a compile error
patterns.name: invalid.illegal.unknown-escape.hero

interpolated.comment: spec § 2: an `f` touching the opening quote makes `{e}` a hole, any expression, ended by the `}` that closes it with nested brackets and literals skipped; `{{` and `}}` each write one brace, and a `}` alone in the text is an error (panel 184 R1, ratified 2026-10-01). This grammar had no rule for the form until 2026-10-02 (`.claude/rules/diagnostics-and-goldens.md` measured it so on 2026-09-10), so a hole's code was painted as text and a quote inside a hole ended the string. The `spec/colouring` check holds the two brace escapes and the lone brace against what the compiler's own lexer accepts and refuses (`selfhost/lex_interp.hero`). Since 2026-10-12 it ends at its line's end too, as a string does, and paints a raw tab or control character in its text.
interpolated.name: string.quoted.double.interpolated.hero

interpolation-hole.comment: A hole of an `f` literal: ordinary code up to the `}` that closes it, its content `meta.embedded` so a theme paints it as code rather than as the string around it, a `{ }` inside it (a map literal) taken whole so its `}` closes nothing early, and a literal inside it read as the literal it is, through `$self`. It ends at its line's end too since 2026-10-12, where the lexer ends the literal.
interpolation-hole.name: meta.interpolation.hero

backtick.comment: A string in backticks, or a backtick alone to its line's end, which the lexer refuses as `unexpected_character` and tells to write the string in double quotes.
backtick.name: invalid.illegal.backtick.hero

char.comment: one ASCII character or one escape; its value is an int (§4.3). The escape class carried `[nt\\']` until 2026-09-13 and so painted `'\r'` as `invalid.illegal.char-literal.hero` by falling through to the third pattern — the same missing `r` as in the string rule above, in the second of the two places it had to be written by hand. The second pattern took every printable character until 2026-10-12, the quote and the backslash with them, so `'''` and `'\'`, both refused by the lexer, were painted as characters; it leaves both out now. The third pattern is written as it always was, and the check splits the file on its text.

number.comment: spec § 2 and `selfhost/number.hero`, first match wins: an uppercase base prefix and a based literal with a fraction are refused, then the three bases, then a based literal the lexer refuses (no digit, a digit of another base, a misplaced `_`), an exponent, a misplaced `_` in a decimal literal, a float (a leading zero allowed before its point), a leading zero, and an integer. Text the lexer reads as several tokens, `1u8` or `1._5`, is painted as neither one literal nor an error. Until 2026-10-12 this read `[0-9]+` alone, so `1_000` and every based literal went unpainted and `07` and `1e5` were painted as numbers. The `spec/colouring` check runs these rules on each form against the lexer.

slashes.comment: `//` is refused wherever it stands outside a string or a comment, `unexpected_character`: a comment begins with `#`, and an integer is divided by `/`.
slashes.name: invalid.illegal.slashes.hero

operator.comment: `selfhost/punctuation.hero`'s table, the longest first: its two-byte operators, then the one-byte ones. `<<` `>>` and `&` `^` `~` joined on 2026-10-12, spec § 7's bitwise row.
